minutes.headline: Town Meeting let the Select Board override the commission's rulings on town buildings; the commission plans to keep pressing on the old primary school.
minutes.summary: The Architectural Preservation District Commission met remotely and approved its April minutes. Most of the meeting reviewed Town Meeting, where the Select Board gained the power to take commission rulings on town buildings to Town Meeting. An amendment giving homeowners the same right was voted down. Members then discussed the old primary school, the Brooks House and other endangered properties, and planned follow-up with the Select Board and Planning Board. The meeting adjourned.

votes.motion: Accept the minutes of the April meeting as written

budget_items.topic: Site plan study for open green space at the old primary school property
budget_items.what_was_said: Town Meeting approved an article for a site plan study of green space on the primary school property; the amount was confirmed in discussion.

budget_items.topic: Community Preservation Act money for restoring old buildings
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted other communities have used CPA money to restore small buildings like the Brooks House.

decisions.decision: The chair will check Planning Board meeting dates and try to schedule another joint meeting about the Brooks House.
The commission will send a letter, possibly with a postcard or photo, urging the Methodist church owners to restore the steeple.
A member intends to make another presentation to the Select Board on the old primary school.
The chair will contact the former Select Board member about the green space plan to try to retain the old primary building.
The next meeting is set for Wednesday June 23rd, remote.

what_happened.line: Town Meeting gave the Select Board power to take commission rulings on town buildings to Town Meeting; an amendment giving homeowners the same right was voted down.
Town Meeting approved an article for a site plan study of green space at the old primary school property.
A member intends to present to the Select Board again on the old primary school, and the chair will contact a former Select Board member about the green space plan.
The chair will try to schedule another joint meeting with the Planning Board about the Brooks House.
The commission approved its April minutes, plans a letter urging the Methodist church owners to restore the steeple, and set its next meeting for June 23.

why_it_matters: Rulings by this commission on town-owned buildings, such as the old primary school, can now be taken to Town Meeting, so residents may be asked to vote on whether a preservation decision stands.
The green space study approved at Town Meeting bears on whether the old primary school building is kept or cleared, and on how public land there is used.
watch_next: Next commission meeting, Wednesday June 23, held remotely.
The commission's follow-up with the Select Board on the old primary school and with the Planning Board on the Brooks House.
